title: MetaData.reflect does not pass dialect-specific kwargs to inspector in Oracle, so oracle_resolve_synonyms is ignored

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Describe the bug

When calling 
```MetaData.reflect(bind=engine, oracle_resolve_synonyms=True)``` in the Oracle dialect, 
`available: util.OrderedSet[str] = util.OrderedSet(insp.get_table_names(schema))` returns an empty list, so load variable is also empty via 
`if only is None: load = [name for name, schname in zip(available, available_w_schema) if extend_existing or schname not in current]`. 
Meanwhile, 
`_reflect_info = insp._get_reflection_info(schema=schema, filter_names=load, available=available, kind=kind, scope=util.preloaded.engine_reflection.ObjectScope.ANY, **dialect_kwargs)` 
is correct and valid, but at the end of the function,
 `for name in load: Table(name, self, **reflect_opts)` is skipped because `load` is empty. 
As a result, synonym tables are not reflected, even though they exist and are visible in `_reflect_info`.


### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

sqlalchemy==2.0.43

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

https://python-oracledb.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

### Database Vendor and Major Version

Oracle Database 18c XE

### Python Version

3.13.3

### Operating system

MacOS

### To Reproduce

# 1. Pull the Oracle XE Docker image
`docker pull gvenzl/oracle-xe`

# 2. Run the container
`docker run -d --name oracle-xe -p 1521:1521 -e ORACLE_PASSWORD=MySecretPass gvenzl/oracle-xe
`
# 3. Connect to the container as SYSTEM user
`docker exec -it oracle-xe sqlplus system/MySecretPass@XE`

Inside SQL*Plus, run the following SQL commands:
# 4. Create the owner user
```
CREATE USER owner_user IDENTIFIED BY test;
GRANT CONNECT, RESOURCE TO owner_user;
```

# 5. Create tables as owner_user
```
ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = owner_user;

CREATE TABLE person (
    id NUMBER PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR2(100)
);
```

# 6. Create a new read-only user
```
CREATE USER test_reader IDENTIFIED BY test;
GRANT CONNECT TO test_reader;
```

# 7. Grant SELECT on owner_user tables
`GRANT SELECT ON owner_user.person TO test_reader;`

# 8. Switch to SYSTEM to allow SELECT on synonyms
`CONNECT system/MySecretPass@XE;`

# 9. Create synonyms for owner_user tables
`CREATE SYNONYM person FOR owner_user.person;`

# 10. Grant SELECT privileges on synonyms
`GRANT SELECT ON person TO test_reader;`

# 11. Grant SELECT ANY DICTIONARY to test_reader (to allow full reflection)
`GRANT SELECT ANY DICTIONARY TO test_reader;`

# 12. Connect as test_reader and verify
```
CONNECT test_reader/test@XE;

SELECT * FROM person;
SELECT * FROM sth;
```

this is working in the SQL.
Now setup properly the connection string in python and connect to the database using the SQLAlchemy.

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, MetaData, Table
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine

# Oracle XE connection string
# Make sure Docker container is running and port 1521 is mapped
engine: Engine = create_engine("oracle+cx_oracle://test_reader:test@localhost:1521/XE")

metadata = MetaData()
metadata.reflect(bind=engine, oracle_resolve_synonyms=True)

print("Reflected tables:")
for table_name in metadata.tables:
    print(table_name)


# There is no output, but there should be reflection of the synonym person which i linked above.

# My small fix for my purposes is this but its not robust, just low hanging fruit to make it work.



# Handle the specific use-case with Oracle synonyms
if dialect_kwargs.get("oracle_resolve_synonyms"):
    available: util.OrderedSet[str] = util.OrderedSet(
        insp.get_table_names(schema, oracle_resolve_synonyms=True)
    )
else:
    available = util.OrderedSet(insp.get_table_names(schema))
```

### Error

There is no error which causes exception or etc, the error is that executing the code above is not printed any output.
